hero_description: I build scalable, mobile-first digital experiences for the web.
meta_title: Javier Chi · Senior AI Software Engineer · Next.js · SaaS · AI Automation
meta_description: Senior software engineer with 6+ years building SaaS platforms, AI-powered automations, and production web products. Currently Senior Full Stack Engineer at Brania.
about_paragraph_1: I'm a senior software engineer who builds products with AI. Right now I'm building Brania, an AI-powered platform, as a Senior Full Stack Engineer: I design and ship complete features, from frontend to backend.
about_paragraph_2: In parallel I run Lab2Next, my own SaaS for clinical labs. I designed, built and launched it on my own, and I keep it running in production, from product and infrastructure to support.
about_paragraph_3: Over 6+ years I've shipped production software for clients in the US and Latin America: data-intensive portals, multi-tenant platforms, and a legacy BI migration to Spark + Superset. I work mostly with React, Next.js, TypeScript and Node, and I own the full cycle, from spec to post-launch maintenance.
about_paragraph_personal: I am a software engineer in Mérida, Mexico, working with clients and teams in the US and Latin America. I like to stay close to the problem: understand how the people who will use the software work before writing the first line, and stay after launch.
about_paragraph_4: Away from code I practice Shotokan Karate (2nd Dan) and play exploration and fantasy games. Karate and software taught me the same things: clarity, discipline and getting a little better every day.
about_quote: I fear not the man who has practiced 10,000 kicks once, but I fear the man who has practiced one kick 10,000 times.

Regulated loan management platform for US lending operations across multiple state jurisdictions.

Built jurisdiction-configurable form rules: one codebase enforcing state-by-state regulatory requirements without forking. Contributed to a multi-quarter .NET legacy migration and took end-to-end ownership of triage: bugs, new form fields, and registration logic in a regulated environment.
